# Phase 6: Monitoring & Support

**Version:** 1.0  
**Last Updated:** 2026-02-09  
**Phase Number:** 6 of 7

## Duration Estimates by Project Type

| Project Type | Duration | Complexity |
|-------------|----------|------------|
| POC | 1-2 weeks | Low |
| Prototype | 2-4 weeks | Low-Medium |
| MVP | 4-8 weeks | Medium-High |
| Handover | 8-12+ weeks | High |

## Description

Phase 6 ensures the deployed application runs smoothly in production through continuous monitoring, performance optimization, incident response, user support, and ongoing maintenance. This phase continues until project closure or handover to a permanent operations team.

## Objectives

- ✓ Monitor application health and performance continuously
- ✓ Respond to incidents quickly and effectively
- ✓ Provide user support and resolve issues
- ✓ Optimize performance based on real-world usage
- ✓ Track and analyze system metrics and KPIs
- ✓ Implement minor enhancements and bug fixes
- ✓ Collect and act on user feedback
- ✓ Maintain system stability and uptime
- ✓ Prepare for project closure or handover

---

## 1. Phase Overview

### Purpose
Ensure the application remains stable, performant, and available while providing support to users and continuously improving the system based on real-world usage and feedback.

### Goals
1. **System Health:** Maintain system uptime and performance targets
2. **Incident Response:** Quickly identify and resolve issues
3. **User Support:** Provide timely support to users
4. **Performance Optimization:** Continuously improve system performance
5. **Feedback Integration:** Collect and act on user feedback
6. **Continuous Improvement:** Implement enhancements and fixes
7. **Documentation:** Maintain up-to-date operational documentation
8. **Stability:** Ensure consistent, reliable service delivery

### Success Criteria
- ✓ System uptime meets SLA (typically 99.9% for MVP/Handover)
- ✓ Incident response time within SLA
- ✓ User satisfaction score ≥8/10
- ✓ Performance metrics within targets
- ✓ All critical incidents resolved
- ✓ Support backlog managed effectively
- ✓ System improvements implemented
- ✓ Comprehensive operational documentation maintained

---

## 2. Prerequisites

### From Phase 5 (Deployment)
- ✓ Application successfully deployed to production
- ✓ Monitoring and alerting operational
- ✓ Operations runbook complete
- ✓ Smoke tests passing
- ✓ No critical deployment issues
- ✓ Deployment sign-off obtained
- ✓ Support team briefed

### Operational Prerequisites
- ✓ Monitoring dashboards accessible
- ✓ Alerting system configured
- ✓ Logging infrastructure operational
- ✓ Incident management system ready
- ✓ Support ticketing system configured
- ✓ On-call schedule established
- ✓ Escalation procedures documented
- ✓ Backup and recovery systems tested

### Resource Prerequisites
- ✓ Support team identified and trained
- ✓ On-call engineers assigned
- ✓ DevOps support available
- ✓ Development team accessible for critical issues
- ✓ Communication channels established
- ✓ User support channels operational

## 5. Sub-Phases

### Sub-Phase 6.1: Initial Monitoring Period (Week 1)

**Activities:**
- Monitor system intensively
- Establish baseline metrics
- Fine-tune alerting thresholds
- Address immediate issues
- Collect initial user feedback
- Document common issues
- Optimize as needed

**Outputs:**
- Baseline performance metrics
- Initial issues identified and resolved
- Refined monitoring configuration
- Initial feedback collected

**Duration by Type:**
- POC: 2-3 days
- Prototype: 3-5 days
- MVP: 5-7 days
- Handover: 7-10 days

### Sub-Phase 6.2: Stabilization & Optimization (Weeks 2-3)

**Activities:**
- Continue monitoring
- Implement performance optimizations
- Fix identified bugs
- Improve monitoring and alerting
- Respond to user feedback
- Optimize resource utilization
- Update documentation

**Outputs:**
- Performance improvements
- Bug fixes deployed
- Optimized monitoring
- Updated documentation

**Duration by Type:**
- POC: 3-5 days
- Prototype: 5-10 days
- MVP: 10-14 days
- Handover: 14-21 days

### Sub-Phase 6.3: Steady-State Operations (Weeks 3+)

**Activities:**
- Ongoing monitoring
- Incident response as needed
- User support
- Minor enhancements
- Performance tuning
- Regular maintenance
- Reporting
- Feedback integration

**Outputs:**
- Stable system operations
- Resolved incidents
- Implemented enhancements
- Regular reports

**Duration by Type:**
- POC: Minimal (0-3 days)
- Prototype: 3-7 days
- MVP: 14-28 days
- Handover: 28-56+ days

### Sub-Phase 6.4: Handover Preparation (Final 1-2 weeks for Handover projects)

**Activities:**
- Prepare handover documentation
- Train operations team
- Conduct knowledge transfer sessions
- Create transition plan
- Test operational procedures
- Establish support continuity

**Outputs:**
- Handover documentation complete
- Operations team trained
- Transition plan ready

**Duration:**
- POC: N/A
- Prototype: N/A
- MVP: Optional
- Handover: 7-14 days

## 7. Quality Gates

### Entry Criteria

Before starting Phase 6:
- ✓ Phase 5 exit criteria met
- ✓ Application stable in production
- ✓ Monitoring operational
- ✓ Support systems ready
- ✓ On-call schedule established

### In-Progress Checkpoints

#### Checkpoint 1: Week 1 Review (End of Sub-Phase 6.1)
**Criteria:**
- ✓ System stable for 7 days
- ✓ Baseline metrics established
- ✓ No critical outstanding incidents
- ✓ Monitoring and alerting validated
- ✓ Initial issues addressed

**Actions if Not Met:**
- Extend monitoring period
- Address stability issues
- Refine monitoring

#### Checkpoint 2: Month 1 Review (End of Sub-Phase 6.2)
**Criteria:**
- ✓ System uptime meets SLA
- ✓ Performance optimized
- ✓ User feedback positive
- ✓ Support processes working
- ✓ Team comfortable with operations

**Actions if Not Met:**
- Investigate stability issues
- Improve support processes
- Additional training

### Exit Criteria

Phase 6 is complete when transitioning to Phase 7 (Closure) or when:

#### System Health
- ✓ System uptime meets SLA (target: 99.9%)
- ✓ Performance metrics within targets
- ✓ No critical outstanding incidents
- ✓ Error rates within acceptable range
- ✓ System stable for minimum monitoring period

#### Support & Incidents
- ✓ All critical incidents resolved
- ✓ High-priority incidents resolved or scheduled
- ✓ Incident response time within SLA
- ✓ Support backlog manageable
- ✓ User satisfaction ≥8/10

#### Documentation
- ✓ Runbooks up-to-date
- ✓ Incident documentation complete
- ✓ Known issues documented
- ✓ Troubleshooting guides current
- ✓ Operational procedures documented

#### Knowledge Transfer (Handover projects)
- ✓ Operations team trained
- ✓ Knowledge transfer sessions complete
- ✓ Handover documentation complete
- ✓ Operations team confident and capable
- ✓ Support continuity ensured

#### Approvals
- ✓ DevOps sign-off on system health
- ✓ Product Manager sign-off on user satisfaction
- ✓ Stakeholder approval to close/handover
- ✓ Go/No-Go decision for Phase 7

## 8. Testing Requirements

### Continuous Monitoring

**System Health Checks:**
- Application availability (uptime)
- Response times
- Error rates
- Resource utilization (CPU, memory, disk)
- Database performance
- API endpoint health

**Automated Checks:**
- Synthetic transactions
- Health endpoint monitoring
- Service dependency checks
- SSL certificate expiration
- Disk space monitoring

### Incident Testing

**Post-Fix Verification:**
- Regression testing after bug fixes
- Performance testing after optimizations
- Smoke tests after deployments
- Load testing after scaling

### Disaster Recovery Testing

**Recommended Frequency:**
- POC/Prototype: Optional
- MVP: Quarterly
- Handover: Monthly

**Tests:**
- Backup restoration
- Failover procedures
- Recovery time objectives (RTO)
- Recovery point objectives (RPO)

### Incident Reports

**Location:** `logs/{project_id}/phase_6_monitoring/incidents/`  
**Frequency:** Per incident (critical/high priority)

**Format:**
```markdown
# Incident Report: INC-001

**Incident ID:** INC-001
**Date:** YYYY-MM-DD
**Time Detected:** HH:MM UTC
**Time Resolved:** HH:MM UTC
**Duration:** X hours Y minutes
**Severity:** Critical | High | Medium | Low
**Status:** Open | Investigating | Resolved | Closed

## Summary
Brief description of the incident

## Impact
- Users affected: X
- Services impacted: [List]
- Business impact: [Description]

## Timeline
- HH:MM - Incident detected via [alert/user report]
- HH:MM - Investigation started
- HH:MM - Root cause identified
- HH:MM - Fix implemented
- HH:MM - Incident resolved
- HH:MM - Verification complete

## Root Cause
Detailed explanation of what caused the incident

## Resolution
Steps taken to resolve the incident

## Prevention
Actions to prevent recurrence:
- [ ] Action 1
- [ ] Action 2

## Lessons Learned
Key takeaways from this incident
```

## 12. Risk Management

### Common Risks in Phase 6

#### Risk 1: Unexpected Downtime
**Probability:** Medium  
**Impact:** Critical  
**Mitigation:**
- Robust monitoring and alerting
- On-call coverage
- Disaster recovery plan
- Regular backups
- High availability architecture

**Response:** Execute incident response procedures, engage on-call team

#### Risk 2: Performance Degradation
**Probability:** Medium  
**Impact:** High  
**Mitigation:**
- Continuous performance monitoring
- Capacity planning
- Performance testing
- Optimization plans ready
- Scaling capabilities

**Response:** Investigate, optimize, scale resources if needed

#### Risk 3: Security Incident
**Probability:** Low  
**Impact:** Critical  
**Mitigation:**
- Security monitoring
- Regular security updates
- Access controls
- Incident response plan
- Security training

**Response:** Execute security incident response, engage security team

#### Risk 4: Data Loss
**Probability:** Low  
**Impact:** Critical  
**Mitigation:**
- Regular automated backups
- Backup verification
- Disaster recovery testing
- Data replication
- Point-in-time recovery

**Response:** Execute recovery procedures, restore from backup

#### Risk 5: Support Overload
**Probability:** Medium  
**Impact:** Medium  
**Mitigation:**
- Adequate support staffing
- Self-service documentation
- Prioritization system
- Escalation procedures
- Knowledge base

**Response:** Triage ruthlessly, add temporary support resources

#### Risk 6: Skill Gaps in Operations Team
**Probability:** Medium (Handover)  
**Impact:** High  
**Mitigation:**
- Comprehensive training
- Documentation
- Shadowing periods
- Gradual handover
- Support access after handover

**Response:** Extended handover period, additional training

## 13. Success Metrics & KPIs

### System Performance Metrics

| Metric | Target (MVP/Handover) |
|--------|----------------------|
| Uptime/Availability | 99.9% (three nines) |
| API Response Time (p95) | <500ms |
| Page Load Time (p95) | <3 seconds |
| Error Rate | <0.1% |
| Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR) | <30 minutes |

### Incident Management Metrics

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Critical Incident Response Time | <15 minutes |
| Critical Incident Resolution Time | <2 hours |
| High-Priority Incident Response Time | <30 minutes |
| High-Priority Incident Resolution Time | <4 hours |
| Incident Recurrence Rate | <5% |

### Support Metrics

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Support Ticket Response Time | <4 hours (business hours) |
| Support Ticket Resolution Time | <24 hours (avg) |
| User Satisfaction Score | ≥8/10 |
| First Contact Resolution Rate | ≥70% |
| Support Backlog | <20 open tickets |

### Resource Utilization Metrics

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| CPU Utilization | <70% (avg) |
| Memory Utilization | <80% (avg) |
| Disk Utilization | <75% |
| Network Utilization | <60% (avg) |

### Cost Metrics

| Metric | Tracking |
|--------|----------|
| Infrastructure Cost/User | Monitor and optimize |
| Cost Trend | Stable or decreasing |
| Cost vs. Budget | Within ±10% |

## 14. Exit Criteria

### System Health
- ✓ Uptime meets SLA for minimum period (4 weeks for MVP, 8 weeks for Handover)
- ✓ Performance metrics consistently within targets
- ✓ No critical outstanding incidents
- ✓ Error rates within acceptable range
- ✓ Resource utilization stable and optimized

### Support & User Satisfaction
- ✓ User satisfaction score ≥8/10
- ✓ All critical support issues resolved
- ✓ Support backlog manageable (<20 tickets)
- ✓ Common issues documented
- ✓ Self-service resources available

### Incident Management
- ✓ All critical incidents resolved and documented
- ✓ Root causes addressed
- ✓ Preventive measures implemented
- ✓ Incident response procedures tested
- ✓ Mean time to recovery within SLA

### Documentation
- ✓ Operations runbook complete and current
- ✓ All incidents documented
- ✓ Troubleshooting guides updated
- ✓ System documentation current
- ✓ Known issues documented

### Operational Readiness
- ✓ Monitoring and alerting optimized
- ✓ Backup and recovery tested
- ✓ Disaster recovery plan validated
- ✓ On-call procedures working
- ✓ Team trained and confident

### Handover (Handover projects only)
- ✓ Operations team fully trained
- ✓ Knowledge transfer complete
- ✓ Handover documentation complete
- ✓ Support continuity ensured
- ✓ Operations team sign-off obtained

### Approvals
- ✓ DevOps Engineer sign-off
- ✓ Product Manager sign-off
- ✓ Technical Architect approval
- ✓ Operations team sign-off (Handover)
- ✓ Stakeholder approval to close
- ✓ Go/No-Go decision for Phase 7

## 15. Phase Transition

### Transition to Phase 7: Project Closure

#### Pre-Transition Activities
1. Validate all Phase 6 exit criteria
2. Complete final reports
3. Conduct handover (if applicable)
4. Archive operational data
5. Prepare closure documentation

#### Handover Activities (Handover Projects)

**Handover Package:**
- Complete system documentation
- Operations runbooks
- Incident history and lessons learned
- Performance baselines
- Support knowledge base
- Contact information
- Training materials
- Transition plan

**Handover Meeting:**
1. System overview and architecture (30 min)
2. Operations procedures (45 min)
3. Monitoring and incident response (30 min)
4. Support processes (20 min)
5. Q&A and shadowing plan (25 min)

**Shadowing Period:**
- Week 1: Operations team shadows project team
- Week 2: Project team shadows operations team (reverse shadowing)
- Week 3-4: Gradual handover with support available
- Week 5+: Full handover with on-call backup

## 18. Common Pitfalls

### Pitfall 1: Inadequate Monitoring
**Prevention:** Comprehensive monitoring from day 1  
**Recovery:** Immediately add missing monitoring

### Pitfall 2: Slow Incident Response
**Prevention:** Clear escalation procedures, on-call coverage  
**Recovery:** Improve incident response process

### Pitfall 3: Poor Documentation
**Prevention:** Document as you go  
**Recovery:** Dedicated documentation sprint

### Pitfall 4: Ignoring User Feedback
**Prevention:** Regular feedback collection and review  
**Recovery:** Prioritize user feedback immediately

### Pitfall 5: Insufficient Handover (Handover projects)
**Prevention:** Structured handover process with training  
**Recovery:** Extended support period

---

## 19. Best Practices

### Monitoring
1. Monitor business metrics, not just technical
2. Set up meaningful alerts (avoid alert fatigue)
3. Use dashboards for visibility
4. Track trends over time
5. Continuous improvement of monitoring

### Incident Management
1. Document every incident
2. Conduct root cause analysis
3. Implement preventive measures
4. Learn from incidents
5. Practice incident response

### Support
1. Prioritize ruthlessly
2. Build knowledge base from common issues
3. Empower users with self-service
4. Set and communicate SLAs
5. Collect user feedback continuously

### Communication
1. Regular status updates
2. Transparent reporting
3. Proactive stakeholder communication
4. Celebrate improvements
5. Share lessons learned

### Optimization
1. Continuous performance monitoring
2. Data-driven optimization
3. Cost optimization
4. Regular review and improvement
5. Balance performance with cost
